audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Yasuo Levels 2 and 3 and mark Level 6 neutral, while early opens 'Levels 1-3 are yours', whys[1] calls Level 2 a burst 'he cannot match', and whys[4] says The Culling executes him.
audit.why: Yasuo has no Wind Wall until 2 and it is a 25s cooldown at rank 1 for four seconds of cover; Lucian out-ranges him at 1 and his Level 2 Q into Lightslinger lands before Steel Tempest can reach two stacks.
audit.corrected: Levels 1, 2, 3 and 6 flipped to Lucian in both layers with matching ratings; Levels 4-5 stays Skill and both item rows stay Yasuo.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why credits The Culling generically without the one condition that decides it, and dosFull[2].d invents a 'fifteen-second invitation' for Wind Wall.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 falling to 17s at rank 5 — never fifteen — and a held wall blanks the entire Culling channel, so the ult is only a spike when the wall is spent.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now carries the real Wind Wall cooldown; dosFull[2].d replaced entirely.

audit.whatIsWrong: Way of the Wanderer's shield appears nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Yasuo builds a shield whenever he is moving and it triggers on the first damage he takes from a champion — it eats the front of exactly the burst string Lucian opens with, so the first shot is a shield-breaker, not damage.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d now states the passive shield and what to do about it.
sources: brief enemyKit P text + shield flag

audit.why: The Wind Wall interaction itself is stated correctly and prominently — it blocks Lucian's Q, W, R and his ranged basic attacks, all four of which the kit data flags as projectiles. Nothing to fix there.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer writes 'Windwall' as one word throughout, and never names Steel Tempest or Last Breath (flagged in packet defects).
audit.why: The ability is Wind Wall; using the real names of Steel Tempest and Last Breath makes the knockup-into-ult sequence readable instead of 'his Q' and 'his R'.
audit.corrected: Spelling fixed and real names used in the fields edited here.

edits.before: The Culling adds lane-clear and execute chip — use it through walls on recalls and low-HP escapes.
edits.after: The Culling executes him, but only into a spent Wind Wall — 21s at rank 3, and it eats the channel.

edits.before: Yasuo burns Wind Wall on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Way of the Wanderer shields him on the move — break it, then burst.

edits.before: His first crit item plus R coming online flips the trade — Windwall now reliably blanks your Q and Culling.
edits.after: His first crit item flips the trade — Wind Wall drops toward 17s and reliably blanks your Q and Culling.

edits.before: He hard-outscales you: crit DPS, a Windwall that eats every projectile, and a knockup-into-R that bursts your squishy frame.
edits.after: He hard-outscales you: crit DPS, a Wind Wall that eats every projectile, and Last Breath off any knockup deletes you.

edits.before: The Culling can execute a Yasuo who burned his dash and W on the wave, but bait Windwall first or the channel gets eaten.
edits.after: The Culling can execute a Yasuo who burned his dash and W on the wave, but bait Wind Wall first or the channel is eaten.

edits.before: His biggest window: with crit items and R up he flash-Q knockups onto you and Windwall blanks your Culling and Q poke.
edits.after: His biggest window: with crit items up, a stacked Steel Tempest knockup chains Last Breath and Wind Wall blanks your poke.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours. You out-range him at level 1 and your Q-into-Lightslinger double shot wins the first trade before his Q can build toward a knockup. The trap is his Windwall — if he drops it your whole Q is wasted, so throw a cheap Q to bait it or just step up and auto when it is on cooldown. At 3 you have W to mark him for the move-speed burst and E to dash out, so kite his E dash-in and punish him every time he steps up to last-hit.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours. You out-range him at level 1 and your Q-into-Lightslinger double shot wins the first trade before Steel Tempest can build toward a knockup. The trap is Wind Wall — four seconds that eat your Q, your W and your autos — so throw a cheap Q to bait it and step in while it sits on its 25s rank-1 cooldown. At 3 you have W to mark him for the move-speed burst and E to dash out, so kite his dash-in and punish every last-hit.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are where it tightens. He has more sustain and his Q is closer to a charged knockup, so don't sit in his E-Q range and feed him a stack for free. Keep using W's mark and your move-speed to stay at the tip of your auto range. At 6 The Culling is a real all-in if he has wasted his dash or his Windwall is down — but a held Windwall blanks the whole channel, so never open The Culling into a fresh wall.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are where it tightens. He has more sustain and Steel Tempest is closer to a charged knockup, so don't sit in his dash range and feed him a stack for free. Keep using W's mark and your move-speed to stay at the tip of your auto range. At 6 The Culling is a real all-in if he has spent his dash or Wind Wall is down — but a held wall blanks the whole channel, so never open into a fresh one.

edits.before: This is his game now. Once Yasuo hits crit items his Windwall is up every fight to eat your Q and The Culling, and a single E-flash or stacked Q knockup chains into his R and deletes your low base HP before E resets. You are a weak scaler for the role and he is the opposite. Get your lead in the first six levels, take plates and roam, and never 1v1 a fed Yasuo into his Windwall — make him fight your team, not you.
edits.after: This is his game now. Once Yasuo hits crit items Wind Wall is a 17-second cooldown eating your Q, your autos and The Culling for four seconds of every fight, and a stacked Steel Tempest knockup chains Last Breath through your low base HP. You are a weak scaler for the role and he is the opposite. Get your lead in the first six levels, take plates and roam, and never 1v1 a fed Yasuo — make him fight your team.

edits.before: Bait his Windwall with a throwaway Q, then commit your real Q and The Culling once it is down
edits.after: Bait Wind Wall with a throwaway Q, then commit the real Q and The Culling while it is down

edits.before: Hold Windwall to eat your Q, W and The Culling at the key moment of every trade
edits.after: Hold Wind Wall to eat your Q, W and The Culling at the key moment of a trade

notes: Wind Wall's placement rules — whether it blocks a Culling already channelling if dropped mid-cast, and whether it stops the shots or only new ones — are not in Riot's text, so the page says only that a wall held before you open blanks the channel. Yasuo's E cooldown reads 0.5/0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 in the kit file (the per-target dash cooldown), which is why no E cooldown number appears in the advice.
